plain: In the late 1940s and 1950s, people in New Mexico reported strange green fireballs crossing the sky, and the government set up an investigation called Project Twinkle to find out what they were. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes it as an investigation run by the "Z division" of Sandia, a nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico. Michels tells it in two episodes and calls it an Air Force project. He says it was led by Lincoln LaPaz, a meteor expert at the University of New Mexico, who began to track the green fireballs. In one telling Michels points to FBI documents about the fireballs. In an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, he says the fireballs showed up across American nuclear sites, naming Los Alamos, where the atomic bomb was built, and Holloman Air Force Base. The tellers raise it because something unexplained seemed drawn to the country's most sensitive nuclear sites just as the bomb age began.
